messages:
natalie: Heads-up — spot check found 3 service accounts with broad roles granted to old terraform user group. looks like leftovers from the initial infra migration.

sam: Ugh. Which roles? can you paste the query result?

natalie: pasted results below from the iam-audit query:
```sql
SELECT member, role, resource FROM iam_bindings
WHERE member LIKE '%tf-deploy%' AND role LIKE 'roles/%admin%';
```

natalie: output: `tf-deploy-sa@proj: roles/editor` on 2 buckets, `tf-deploy-sa@proj: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on 1 key

maria: That KMS role is scary if it's on a production key. Do we know key names/owners?

natalie: key is `projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/customer-data` — owner is old data-team alias.

jason: tagging @ops-oncall — we should rotate the key and revoke the SA immediately but need to coordinate with ingest jobs. can we do a canary removal?

ops-oncall: I can coordinate a 30m maintenance window tonight 23:00 UTC. proposal: remove `cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` from tf-deploy-sa, run smoke ingest, if failures revert via `gcloud iam` quick-restore.

sam: +1. Also we need to add this case to the automated least-privilege audit. current rule set misses `roles/editor` on buckets because we only scan for explicit admin roles.

maria: I can add a new detection for broad roles assigned to service accounts created before 2024-01-01 and flag keys with cross-project bindings. quick patch in the audit lambda: 
```python
# pseudo
broad_roles = ['roles/editor','roles/owner','roles/ownerLegacy']
results = [b for b in bindings if b.role in broad_roles and b.member_type=='serviceAccount']
```

access-review-bot: Automated scan (1816123600): 3 findings. Rule: broad-service-account-roles. Tickets created: SEC-4823, SEC-4824.

natalie: thanks bot — SEC-4823 assigned to @maria, SEC-4824 assigned to @jason.

jason: action plan: 1) schedule tonight rollback window 23:00 UTC 2) remove KMS role from tf-deploy-sa 3) run smoke and integration tests 4) rotate key if any failures or unexpected access logs 5) update terraform to avoid reintroducing role 6) add unit test to infra repo to fail plan when broad roles appear.

sam: re: audit cadence — propose monthly targeted sweep + weekly sampling for high-risk resources (KMS, BigQuery, buckets). keeps ops load manageable.

maria: will PR the detection and a CI check. also adding a small playbook snippet for oncall: commands to list principals with KMS access and to temporarily block a SA: 
```bash
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --keyring=ingest --project=prod
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding proj --member='serviceAccount:tf-deploy-sa@proj' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

natalie: please add a short note to the audit runbook about verifying audit logs (storage.object.* and cloudkms.*) retention before rotation. we had a near-miss last quarter.

ops-oncall: I'll be on standby tonight. post any blockers in this thread and ping me. :white_check_mark:

jason: creating a short RFC to update RBAC baseline and enforcement hooks — will link once ready: http://go/redwood/sec/rbac-baseline-rfc

maria: PR opened: infra#842. test adds detection + CI fail. cc @natalie for acceptance criteria.

natalie: thanks all. quick wins: remove the editor bindings, block SA from KMS tonight if safe, and merge the audit rule. follow-up: monthly sweep schedule in calendar and add owners for KMS keys with cross-team access.

access-review-bot: Reminder scheduled: next monthly sweep starts 1818714000.

sam: closing loop — please update SEC tickets with post-mortem after tonight.

jason: will do.
